ratings_why.fun: Stamps grow by one a fight and the late cards multiply them by recipients, so the board ramps from flat to hot in a shape I'd enjoy, though the first Spawns feel like losing a fish.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the board is a directional stream: a death at the head pulls the whole run up a step mid-fight, and the fish that reaches the Source turns into a Gift for its neighbours; no tribe today moves units in a fight like this.

verdict_why: The engine works; a few timing and trigger questions (the Warden's repeated Homes, Bradán's pretend Spawns) need clear rules before it can settle.

points.text: Warden of the Hazel Well: say whether every fish that reaches the Source Spawns next turn, and whether one fish can come Home twice in a fight.
Old Bradán: say whether his 'as if they Spawned' triggers Little Jack Gravel, Second-Run Hen and the Warden. If it does, Jack makes an Alevin every fight for free.
The Bailiff of the Weir says 'No Leap', and Llyn Llyw gives your other units Leap. Say which one wins.
Early Spawns are about even (a Grilse becomes a 1/2 Alevin for +2 stats to its neighbours). A Gift of at least +1/+1 at 0 Stamps would make turns 2 to 4 feel like a reward.
Pebble-Carrying Hen is a quiet Tier 4 that only saves half a Stamp count. It could also make that Alevin give its Gift once when played.

standouts.why: Old Kelt turns one empty slot into a Stamp for the whole run and a sure homecoming: a cheap, readable engine that sets up your Tier 3 board.
Mother Redd removes the cost of going home, so veterans keep their Stamps and the run keeps growing. That's a real capstone.
Captain Kype rewards a long cascade with extra attacks and turns red at 3 Stamps. Fun to build toward.

weakest.why: Pebble-Carrying Hen does little on a board that rarely Spawns, and not much more on one that Spawns often.
Brother Grilse is a plain tempo body that you then trade for a 1/2 Alevin when it gets home.
Claw-Marked Cock only pays off in long cascades. For a Tier 5 it does little to set the game's build.

flags.note: Little Jack Gravel with the Warden and Mother Redd can make several Alevins a turn, and so a golden and a Discover almost every turn.
Old Kelt may be the right pick at Tier 3 nearly every game: a Stamp for every fish plus a guaranteed homecoming, for one slot.
'Any number of times a fight' doesn't say how many Spawns follow, or whether a fish can come Home again.
It isn't clear whether his pretend Spawns trigger cards that say 'when one of your Salmon Spawns'.
'No Leap' and Llyn Llyw's 'your other units have Leap' contradict each other.
